q: Viewing aerobic respiration as a system, which correctly lists its inputs and outputs?
options: Inputs: glucose, O2, ADP + Pi. Outputs: CO2, H2O, ATP and heat
Inputs: CO2, H2O, ATP. Outputs: glucose, O2, ADP + Pi and heat
Inputs: glucose, CO2, ATP. Outputs: O2, H2O, ADP + Pi
Inputs: glucose and O2 only. Outputs: ATP only, since all the energy is captured
explanation: C6H12O6 + 6O2 → 6CO2 + 6H2O, coupled to ADP + Pi → ATP. Carbon from the substrate leaves as CO2 (link reaction and Krebs cycle); O2 is reduced to water at the end of the electron transport chain. Because energy transfer is inefficient, heat is also an output – which birds and mammals use to maintain body temperature.
